content.text:
Refactor phase complete. All 13 tests green, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Implementation file: `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-09-04_23-11-22_claim-office-example-mapping_v6.1-hybrid-testlist-scope-fix_opus-5-no-thinking-3/src/claim-office.ts`

## Naming evaluation (done first)

- `itemModifiersOf` — the plural name already describes "all surcharges scoped to one item," which is exactly where the upcoming high-enchantment surcharge belongs. Kept.
- `basePremium` (local in `quote`) — **renamed to `policyBasePremium`**. The file has two distinct notions of base premium (`itemBasePremiumOf` for one item, `policyBasePremiumOf` for the whole policy), and the bare local made it ambiguous which one the initial-assessment surcharge applies to. This matters for the coming policy-wide loyalty/follow-up discounts, where the reader has to see at a glance which base they multiply.
- `alikeItemGroups`, `formsBuildingBlock`, `roundedUpInMHPCOsFavour` — all reveal intent well. Kept.

## Refactoring 2: `alikeItemGroups` (Rule 4, then Rule 3)

Replaced the imperative Map-accumulation loop with a declarative group-by over the known item types:

```ts
const insurableItemTypes = Object.keys(BASE_PREMIUMS) as InsurableItemType[];

const alikeItemGroups = (items: Item[]): Item[][] =>
  insurableItemTypes
    .map((type) => items.filter((item) => item.type === type))
    .filter((alikeItems) => alikeItems.length > 0);
```

The old version did a read-modify-rewrite per item (`groupsByType.set(t, [...(get(t) ?? []), item])`) — incidental bookkeeping that the reader had to simulate mentally to confirm it grouped by type. It was also the only mutating block left in an otherwise declarative file.

### APP mass

Old: 2 constants + 6 bindings + 6 invocations (12) + 1 conditional `??` (4) + 1 loop (5) + 1 assignment via `.set` (6) = **31**
New: 1 constant + 6 bindings + 6 invocations (12) + 0 conditionals + 2 loops (10) + 0 assignments = **29**

Net **31 → 29 (Δ −2)**, and the drop is in the heaviest categories — the assignment and conditional are gone, traded for a cheaper second iteration. The `quote` rename is mass-neutral (13 → 13); it was made purely on Rule 2, which outranks APP.

One deliberate trade-off worth flagging: the new version iterates `items` once per item type rather than once total. For the policy sizes in this domain that is irrelevant, and Rules 2 and 4 favour the clearer form — but it also means grouping is now driven by `BASE_PREMIUMS`, so an unknown item type silently drops out of the groups instead of forming its own. That is invisible today because `InsurableItemType` makes unknown types a compile error, and the spec's "unknown item type → error" test (`it.todo` at line 200) will want an explicit validation path at the boundary anyway. Whoever picks up that test should validate on entry rather than relying on grouping to surface it.
